Verdicts: BENIGN for both supplied archives.

toga-ai 1.0.1115 is the TOGA Technology Claude Code team harness.
Sample SHA256:
713015d90997b8982d6e55e302d0b23f3b04aebedcb661915282d23458feb4a8
Fetched predecessor: pkg:npm/toga-ai@1.0.1114
Predecessor SHA256:
d1586c328bce79417d42620800891b0c9d94682d75ed3a3ada2fecc3a0af7856

The complete tar-member comparison changes only package.json's version and
knowledge/1.0/standards/framework-rules.md. The latter expands guidance about
PHP 8.x null arguments, empty database results, and PHP 7.2-safe library fixes.
There are no added or removed regular members. Every installer, hook, skill,
agent and other executable is byte-identical. All 956 original regular members
also match the supplied extraction. The original rules flag the predecessor
with the same two suspicious traits; the clean-predecessor premise is not
reproducible with this checkout.

Execution: package.json postinstall calls install.js --post-install. main()
discovers an optional existing knowledge clone and may git pull --ff-only.
It calls reportTelemetryEnv() before the postinstall early exit. Unless
TOGA_SKIP_TELEMETRY=1, applyTelemetryEnv() parses ~/.claude/settings.json,
replaces managed OTEL environment keys, preserves unrelated settings, backs
up the old file, then writes and renames a temporary file. Invalid JSON is
left alone. Endpoint and bearer overrides are supported. The default block
enables prompt, assistant-response and tool-detail export, account/session
attribution and a hardcoded authenticated HTTPS collector. These global,
default-on content-export settings are sensitive and justify retaining both
suspicious findings. The installer configures subsequent Claude telemetry;
it does not itself transmit a conversation.

The explicit CLI installs project skills/rules/agents/hooks and knowledge,
merges settings and updates CLAUDE.md. Its registry helper invokes npm view;
initial git clone/init and that registry check are skipped on bare postinstall.
start-gate reads hook payloads and maintains ticket/session workflow gates.
start-helper and commit-helper execute git using argument arrays for the
ticket/commit workflow. These actions fit the declared team harness purpose.
No hidden loader, secret harvesting or concrete unauthorized transfer was
identified. Transparent source, operator overrides, the visible telemetry
status and coherent workflow functionality tip the verdict toward BENIGN.
Deployment authorization and collector ownership are not independently known;
the verdict does not establish that global content collection was consented.

The existing QuickJS installer tracer was run on the supplied installer with
in-memory filesystem and inert process APIs. Creation, setting preservation
and managed replacement, opt-out, invalid JSON, endpoint/token overrides and
idempotent reinstall pass. No real sample execution received host APIs.
Decoded-string inspection finds only three spurious Base64 candidates inside
the ordinary firstInstall identifier and decimal timeout constants; no staged
payload. No toga-ai trait changes were necessary or made.

Schemathesis 4.32.4 is the Python OpenAPI/GraphQL property-based API tester.
Sample SHA256:
61e3c4868e6385da0ae49acb55519527a8025172ae405ef5f87ccc4c1dc539ec
Fetched predecessor: pkg:pypi/schemathesis@4.32.3
Predecessor wheel SHA256:
adf3c7a5b303655051f093ece54997e039d4a3765910b4d6dffb5979f940b40e

forager fetch --all-wheels was used for both exact PyPI releases. Each has one
original wheel, and the fetched 4.32.4 wheel exactly matches the supplied hash.
All 396 original regular members match the supplied extraction. The versioned
dist-info directory changes normally; 135 common source files differ. Reviewed
changes include typing/signature cleanup, shared CLI project-option plumbing,
report/recorder helpers, request-body override handling, serialization and
generation/coverage fixes. No added outbound endpoint, concealed decoder or
automatic payload launch was found in these changes.

The decisive options.py diff adds typing.Any and changes OptionSpec's argument
annotations. Its --auth help string is unchanged:
  Authenticate all API requests with basic authentication
OptionSpec stores args and kwargs, later passed to click.option. validate_auth
splits the user's USER:PASS into a tuple; project override updates AuthConfig.
Configured basic credentials reach the API test's request auth or
HttpBasicAuthProvider, which builds its Authorization header. RequestsTransport
uses the configured/schema API URL and session.request; its session restricts
redirects using requests' credential-stripping decision. It does not send the
help string as a credential. CLI auth defaults do not contain a baked-in
username/password. WFC auth files and dynamic auth are user/config-selected
API testing features. This purpose-aligned data flow and ordinary release diff
tip the verdict toward BENIGN. Authorization to test a particular target is
deployment context not supplied here.

The old case-insensitive basic-auth-credential-literal matcher accepted
Authenticate ... basic authentication: the fourteen-letter English word
authentication satisfied its Base64-character regex. Nearby AUTH = OptionSpec
then satisfied hardcoded-basic-auth-credential. The 4.32.3 original-rules scan
reproduces the same false finding. No decoded strings occur in options.py.

Correction: require a ':' or '=' header delimiter with only punctuation or
whitespace between the header name, delimiter and Basic scheme. Keep the
existing credential length, case-insensitivity, placeholder exclusions,
file/platform scope, severity and consumers. No product-name exclusion,
severity reduction or new duplicate trait was introduced. A basic-auth header
value is supported at the existing authorization-header leaf; no intent or
credential-theft claim was added.

Consumer audit: the atom directly feeds hardcoded-basic-auth-credential;
that composite also feeds headers-auth. Repository exact-reference searches
found no further exact consumers or positive expectations tied to these IDs.
Existing calibration-first-review, WAN credential-injection and CouchDB
rewrite fixtures were inspected before narrowing. Seven existing Python/JS
attack/normal controls retain their entire before/after trait sets. Three
focused map/index/wire positives retain both the notable literal and the
suspicious composite. The actual CLI-help near miss loses both. Run:
  python3 testdata/schemathesis-basic-auth-review/check.py
All eleven controls pass.

Full atomscan runs used --no-update --follow=none --mode slow before and after,
including archive-member results. Root summary:
  toga-ai:       2 suspicious / 430 notable -> 2 suspicious / 430 notable
  Schemathesis:  1 suspicious / 498 notable -> 0 suspicious / 496 notable
Neither has hostile traits. toga-ai's complete file/trait sets are unchanged.
Schemathesis loses only the false Basic-auth atom/composite and the displayed
auth-token-variable-assignment wrapper. The wrapper still matches in
test-rules but is filtered as a low-value any/needs<=1 composite once no
matching parent needs it. Its canonical assignment-source notable remains
in every affected member, including AUTH_BOOTSTRAP constants; no assignment
evidence was removed. No tested attack detection was lost.

The calibrated classifier level remains -1 (BENIGN) for both samples before
and after. The generic model's raw probability for Schemathesis rises from
0.7422469 to 0.856485 after removing the false traits, while its wheel-specific
probability changes from 0.018073648 to 0.018578649. toga-ai is unchanged at
0.8229157 generic / 0.04254201 npm-specific. Raw probabilities do not override
the behavior verdict or justify restoring false traits. The scanner warns
that the v18 model feature spec predates the v19 extractor. There is no new

remain compatible with a BENIGN artifact verdict.
